newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends firmer on bull spreads, demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends firmer on bull spreads, demand.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed firmer on Friday and a contract high was notched in the May as aggressive commercial bull spreading fed into ideas demand remained strong despite high prices, pit sources said.
Soyoil struggled with ideas soymeal demand would continue to outpace soyoil purchases, leaving a glut of soyoil.

Continental Grain was the featured player on the day, bull spreading at least 1,000 lots May/July soymeal. Floor sources disagreed about whether the trade reflected a new position or closed out an existing one.
But the action fed into ideas of strong nearby demand.

Those theories were bolstered by the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure which came in at 24.6 million bushels, at the high end of trade expectations. The pace implied good demand despite heavy soy exports from Brazil, traders said.
Also, U.S. Gulf May CIF soybean values rose by two to three cents per bushel Friday morning. Exporters cited lack of farmer selling and strong processor demand in U.S. markets.
Soymeal closed $3.30 to $0.70 per ton higher with July up $2.40 at $294.30. Soyoil ended 0.12 to 0.02 cent per lb lower with July off 0.04 at 24.70.
Weather was also deemed supportive to new crop months. Forecasts called for cool and wet weather to follow the warm weekend. That scenario suggested soybean plantings would slow.
Trade sources expected Monday's weekly USDA crop progress report to show 20 to 25 percent of the crop seeded as of Sunday, up from nine percent last week.

On the day, SAK Futures bought 500 lots July soymeal and Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each bought 300 July. Smith Barney bought and sold 300 July and Tenco Inc sold 300 July and 100 September, pit sources said.
In soyoil, CIS sold 600 lots July, Cargill Inc sold 300 July and ADM and Central Soya each sold 100 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 26,931. Soyoil volume was pegged at 16,000 lots, against Thursday's 21,302.
